raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Endpoint plugins are documented to support overriding core routes, but core routes are registered first and win during request dispatch. For example, a plugin can register `GET /version` successfully while requests still reach the built-in handler. OpenAPI can meanwhile describe the plugin's handler, so the schema and actual response disagree.

This change replaces earlier HTTP operations when a plugin registers the same path template and method. Other methods remain available, and the last registered plugin operation takes precedence. Plugin hooks still run after core router registration. The OpenAPI cache is also cleared so the schema reflects the routes that handle requests.

The endpoint plugin documentation is updated to describe these rules.

Duplicate-work check on September 26, 2026: searched open and closed endpoint-plugin issues and PRs and found no existing fix for this behavior.

## Test Plan

Run the existing plugin and HTTP status metrics suites against this checkout. `TEST_PYTHON` points to the Python executable in the CPU test environment.

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
"$TEST_PYTHON" -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/plugins_tests/test_endpoint_plugins.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/test_http_status_metrics.py
```

The added cases exercise HTTP dispatch and OpenAPI through FastAPI's ASGI interface, covering core route overrides, hook access to core routes, preservation of other methods, and conflicts between plugins.

## Test Result

- **30 passed**: 18 plugin tests and 12 HTTP status metrics tests.
- All six added regression cases fail on the unpatched baseline, `bbc4ddeca`.
- Pre-commit and mypy-3.12 checks passed for the changed files.

No model evaluation was run; validation covers HTTP routing and OpenAPI generation.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with the implementation and regression tests.

**Nothing blocking.** The comments below are optional suggestions. There is no need to push a fix for them before merging.

<!-- bhrv:69dcdb96cfe4cd78 -->

🟡 (optional) Regenerating an API client from /openapi.json after a plugin overrides one method of a multi-method core route can yield a stale operationId (e.g. a POST-only endpoint still tagged with a `_get`-style id) — base never hit this since a route's methods were never mutated after construction. interface.py:126-130 computes `methods = previous.methods - route.methods` then does `previous = copy(previous); previous.methods = methods`, mutating only `.methods` on the shallow copy. FastAPI's `APIRoute.__init__` already cached `self.unique_id` (used as the OpenAPI operationId when none is set) from the original, full method set via `generate_unique_id`, which picks an arbitrary member of that set as the id suffix; the copy keeps that stale id. …

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

…Fix: after narrowing `previous.methods`, also recompute `operation_id`/`unique_id` on the copy so the schema's operationId matches the method(s) it still serves.

Trigger: a plugin partially overrides a route registered with 2+ HTTP methods on one APIRoute (e.g. `@ router.api_route('/x', methods=['GET','POST'])`) — exactly what the new test test_endpoint_plugin_override_preserves_other_methods in tests/plugins_tests/test_endpoint_plugins.py exercises. At interface.py:126-130, the surviving methods are computed and assigned onto a shallow `copy()` of the old APIRoute, but FastAPI's `self.unique_id = self.operation_id or generate_unique_id(self)` (set once in `__init__` using the pre-mutation full method set, `generate_unique_id` picking `list(route.methods)[0]`) is never recomputed. So the retained route can carry an operationId naming a method it no longer serves once `app.openapi_schema` is rebuilt. The added test checks response codes/bodies and response schemas only, not operationId, so this regression ships unverified.

**Verification:** nit (cosmetic; essentially pre-existing for the affected method). The mechanism is real: interface.py:129-130 does `previous = copy(previous)` (shallow copy.copy) then `previous.methods = methods`. FastAPI computes `self.unique_id = self.operation_id or generate_unique_id_function(self)` once in `APIRoute.__init__`, and default `generate_unique_id` appends… | nit. Real but cosmetic.…

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

 ## Path-prefix convention
 
-There is currently no route conflict enforcement (tracked as a follow-up to RFC [#46565](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46565)). A plugin's `attach_router` can register a path that collides with a core route and routes attached later win. To avoid surprising operators:
+Plugin hooks run after the core routers have been registered. HTTP routes added by plugins replace earlier routes with the same path template and HTTP method, including their OpenAPI description. Methods not overridden by the plugin remain available. When multiple plugins register the same operation, the last registered route takes precedence. Different path templates are not treated as equivalent.
+
+There is currently no rejection of route conflicts (tracked as a follow-up to RFC [#46565](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46565)). To avoid surprising operators:
 
 - Namespace your routes under a distinct prefix, e.g. `/plugins/<plugin-name>/...`, rather than reusing `/v1/...` or other core prefixes
 - Only register routes under a core prefix (like the worked example's `/v1/admin/scheduler_config`) if you specifically intend to override or extend existing behavior and document that clearly for operators allowlisting your plugin
